London, 20<sup>th</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Northam Platinum** might reschedule its Booysendal platinum project on concerns about funding and declining platinum prices after Impala Platinum withdrew its bid for Northam Platinum, controlling shareholder Mvelaphanda Resources said on Friday.  James Wellsted, a spokesman for Mvelaphanda, said the mine might be developed in up to five phases instead of as a single project as the company had intended.   Wellsted said a comprehensive review of the project would be undertaken as part of the extensive viability study that the company had launched last year. This is due to be completed by August or September.  He said breaking down the Booysendal project into phases would delay the build-up to 430 000 ounces of platinum group metals a year and the return on the project would be lower. However, it would be easier to fund.  Last August Northam said developing Booysendal in modules would offer flexibility and reduce potential risks relating to power and water supply.  Justin Froneman, a platinum analyst at Macquarie First South, said that Booysendal might be built in four R2 billion phases over 10 years, instead of as a single R8 billion project over five years.  He said Northam had originally indicated that steady-state levels of production from Booysendal would be reached by the 2014 financial year but, given the change in market conditions, this target now appeared “aggressive”.  He said Booysendal’s steady-state production was now expected to be reached in 2020 rather than 2015. _Source:  Business Report_ 

**Braemore Resources** on Monday stated that a 50% expansion of its 3,2 MW ConRoast smelter, operating in Johannesburg, was under way to meet the increased demand for the smelter technology. Since commissioning in September, the smelter had produced 5 971 oz of PGMs.  Braemore also achieved a recovery rate of 99,52% from the high-chrome content PGM concentrate feed.  The ConRoast facility is capable of processing around 2 000 t of concentrate and other smelter feed a month, and producing PGMs in an iron-nickel alloy at a yearly rate of up to 70 000 oz a year, depending on the feed of the grade.  The smelter had been ramping up capacity since October, and in December alone, the smelter produced 4 024 oz of PGMs from high-chrome content feed, averaging 83 g/t of PGMs and 3% chrome. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Anglo Platinum** on Monday reopened the Rustenburg mine’s shaft, which was closed after fatality last week, spokesman Simon Tebele said.  He was unable to say how production at the Rustenburg operations had been lost.  Tebele said that a full investigation into the incident was still under way, and that results could take some time. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Fiat Group** is negotiating with Chrysler LLC to form a strategic partnership that could include a Fiat equity stake in the ailing U.S. carmaker.  The pact would help Chrysler speed and strengthen its res

tructuring plan.  According to people familiar with the matter in Europe and Detroit, Fiat could give Chrysler access to its mini, small and mid-sized car platforms, engines and transmissions.  If the deal is completed, Fiat would get a 30-35 percent stake in Chrysler in exchange for Fiat’s platform, engines and transmission technology, sources told Automotive News Europe. Fiat would get options to acquire up to 55 percent of the automaker over time, The Wall Street Journal reported.  The Financial Times also reported today that the two companies have signed a memorandum of understanding on the alliance, which could be announced within days. Another source told Automotive News that the agreement was signed on Friday, Jan. 16.  Possible extensions of the Fiat-Chrysler deal could include access for Fiat to Chrysler’s North American manufacturing operations and distribution network. _Source:  Automotive News_
